_note: THE COLONY MANAGEMENT SCREEN'S GEOMETRY, AND THE ONLY PLACE IT IS TYPED. Every rectangle is in the 1920x1080 reference space (core/layout.py). tools/frame_build.py builds the frame from this file plus the master's ring and texture; tools/frame_mask.py renders the windows; tools/frame_holes.py derives the cutout boxes back out of the built frame, and a smoke check asserts holes == mask == boxes.json at every resolution (decision 3). So a rectangle changes HERE and nowhere else, and everything downstream is generated - decision 1 and decision 40.
_gaps_note: EVERY GAP IS ONE OF THE MASTER'S OWN STRUTS, MAPPED BY ROLE - not a spacing chosen here. galaxy_map/assets/frame.png has seven distinct struts and every one carries a lit line on both edges with a moulded ridge between; tools/frame_build.py --profiles measures them. header_list 26 <- the master's header|map strut (31 master px, 26.7 ref): a title bar above the main content. list_band 28 <- map|slot (33 px, 28.4 ref): the main content above the row beneath it. band_sort 29 <- box|slot (34 px, 29.2 ref): a panel above a button row, which is what this gap is and what map|slot is not. in_row 38 <- the slot divider (47 px, 38.9 ref): two elements of ONE row side by side, which is the lower band and is also sort_bar|return_button. Rounded DOWN to the integer in every case, so a rail is never wider than the strut it was measured from. The cost is in doc and in v3_projektstatus.md: the list loses 47 px of height and planet_output 60 of width, and the figure columns lose nothing because the rails that grew are horizontal. A3-DEVIATION, 9 September 2026: header_list is 18 and band_sort 22, NOT the master's 26 and 29. The 15 ref px they give up are what the list needs to hold figure step 3 at 1440p once the figure origin became the original's 4*step below the band top rather than 1 px of plate clearance (colonytrack.figure_step). WHY THESE TWO AND NOT THE LOWER BAND: galaxy_inset's aspect is TRANSCRIBED to a thousandth (128*(506000//128) / 91*(400000//91), movebox.cpp:20-21) and a smoke check holds it there, so the box cannot lose height without losing width - 189 -> 174 forces 239 -> 220 and the drawn map 243x173 -> 220x156, which is 10 % smaller and moves AWAY from an inset that is already well under the original's own. The rails cost no drawn pixel at all. AND THE DEVIATION MOVES TOWARD THE ORIGINAL, WHICH IS WHY IT IS AFFORDABLE: the original's own header-to-list gap is ONE native px (header plates end at native y 32, the first list field is at 31*0 + 34, colsum.cpp:311) = about 3 ref, and its band-to-sort gap is four native px (scan box 354 + 88 = 442, sort buttons at 446, colsum.cpp:267-273) = 12 ref. Our 26 and 29 were both wider than the thing being transcribed; 18 and 22 are still wider. The struts they were measured from are unchanged in the master - what changed is that two of the seven are no longer used at full width, and that is the deviation being recorded rather than the strut table being edited.

_ring_source.tool: threshold sweep, alpha < 8 / 16 / 64, bbox stable at all three
_ring_source.note: THE FAMILY RING, FOUR VALUES, AND THE ASYMMETRY IS THE ARTWORK'S AND NOT AN ERROR. The master's metal is wide at the sides, thin at the top and medium at the bottom; a single number cannot describe it, which is why `bezel` is gone. Measured on the main-screen master because that is what this screen has to sit beside, and mapped to the reference space the same way the running screen maps it - the frame image is stretched over the whole reference area (screen._scale_frame), so each axis scales independently. A HAND-COPIED NUMBER GETS A CHECKER (decision 36): the smoke test re-measures that file with the same sweep and fails if the table and the artwork ever disagree. The shipped colony frame is NOT yet this ring - it measures 100/103/12/70 - and tools/frame_build.py is what makes it so.

_list_columns_note: 302 + 347*3 + 314 + 36 = 1693, the list's own width exactly - the columns ARE the list, with no slack to distribute. THE LIST'S WIDTH DID NOT CHANGE WHEN THE GAPS BECAME RAILS on 7 September 2026: rails are horizontal there, so they cost HEIGHT and not width, and the figure capacity is untouched. CAPACITY IS ASSERTED, NOT NOTED: a figure column must fit at least four unsqueezed figures, which is what the original's widest column (industry, reach 122, pitch 30) fits; 347 reference px fits five, at every resolution, because the column and the pitch scale together. THE BUILDING COLUMN IS DERIVED: the original prints the producing text with BILL::Squeeze_Print_Formatted_Paragraph_(0x200, y, 0x55, 0x16, ...) at colsum.cpp:621 - 85 px of a 640 px screen, 13.3 % - and 13.3 % of 1693 is 225. 314 is wider than the transcription requires; the surplus is the extra HD width that Data's Stage 1 decision sends to the column reservation rather than to wider figure spacing. See colonybuild.py for why the width is a RESERVATION and never a squeeze target. THE THREE JOB COLUMNS ARE UNEQUAL, AND THAT IS TRANSCRIBED, corrected 7 September 2026. They were 347 each by our own choice; COLSUM::Get_Selected_Pop_ (colsum.cpp:1006-1024) passes the column bounds as literals - left_x = 101/236/378 and right_x = that - 10 - so the original's spans are 135/142/134 native px with the WORKERS column the widest. Two independent sources: those literals, and the column separators measured on the live framebuffer of screen 20 at x 99/234/376/510, which agree to +1 px on all three. The ratio 135:142:134 over the unchanged 1041 px reservation gives 342/360/339, so name, building and scroll do not move and the list width is still 1693. CAPACITY IS RE-ASSERTED AT THE NARROWEST COLUMN (339), not at the old uniform 347 - the check is what allows this change, not the arithmetic. THE SCROLL COLUMN IS A TRANSCRIPTION NOW, 9 September 2026, and was the last unsourced number here. It was 36 = 1693 - 302 - 342 - 360 - 339 - 314, the leftover after the other five. The original states it twice and the two agree: the track is native x 621..626 (Add_Scroll_Field_(621, 40, 0, n, 0, n-10, 5, 271, ...) at colsum.cpp:278 counts it exclusively as 5, Draw_Bar_Indicator_'s Fill_(621, y1, 626, y2, 229) at colsum.cpp:759 counts the same rectangle inclusively as 6, corner dots at 621 and 626 at colsum.cpp:767-770), and the arrows start at native x 619 (Add_Button_Field_, colsum.cpp:263-264). The arrow anim's own width is animate::Get_Width_(pic) and lives in the player's LBX, so it is MEASURED and single-source like the No Farming size: native x 619..627 off the original's framebuffer in evidence/colony_summary_native_split.png, whose LEFT edge reproduces the source's 619 exactly, which is what anchors the right one. Nine native px is 27 reference px. THE NINE FREED PX GO TO BUILDING, 314 -> 323, because building is already the declared home of this screen's surplus width (see above) - a residue put somewhere that says why, rather than somewhere that had room. And there is no residue left to distribute at all: since 9 September the six columns are fractions of the list_area cutout (colonytrack.columns), so they tile it exactly at any window size by construction rather than by the last column absorbing a mismatch.
_lower_band_note: Four boxes, flush with the list's own edges at 107 and 1800, with gaps of 38 - THE MASTER'S OWN SLOT DIVIDER, 47 master px, the strut it puts between two buttons of one row. planet_output absorbs what the arithmetic leaves, because it is the only width in the band not fixed by something else: the two 320s are a pair and 253 is locked by the inset's aspect. 107 + 320 + 38 + 686 + 38 + 253 + 38 + 320 = 1800. THE INSET IS NO LONGER SHORTER THAN ITS NEIGHBOURS - 8 September 2026. It was 20 px shorter and centred (725 + 10 = 735) on the reading that its height is fixed by its own aspect; at the band's new 191 the aspect is not what binds. colonyinset.map_rect fits the map into 128:91 isotropically and takes min(w/128, h/91), and with the box 253 wide the WIDTH is the smaller term at every resolution - so the map is the same size at 200 and at 191 and the box may simply fill its band like the other three. It starts to shrink below 183.
_galaxy_inset_note: 253 x 200 IS DERIVED AND CONFIRMED - doc/colony_inset_geometry.md Part 3. The original's inset covers 50.6*M x 40*M world units, whose aspect is 1.2651 at EVERY galaxy size because both divisors are constants and M cancels (movebox.cpp:20-21). 253/200 = 1.2650 against that, so the crop fills the box with no letterbox at any size INCLUDING orion2re's Maximum - the earlier expectation that Maximum letterboxes is WITHDRAWN, and it only did so if the crop were the galaxy rather than the original's coverage. The scale that follows is exactly 5/M reference px per world unit. At 3840x2160 the box is 506 x 400 device px, which is the small galaxy's own world extent at 1:1. DEVIATION - THE BOX IS 239 x 189 SINCE 8 September 2026, WAS 253 x 200, AND ONE STATED PROPERTY IS GONE WITH IT. The list grew 29 ref px so that 2560x1440 could take figure step 3 (see _list_height_note), the 29 came out of the lower band's height, and the band's height is what fixes this box. THE ASPECT RULE SURVIVES and is what the check still asserts: 239/189 = 1.26455 against the coverage's 1.265134, 0.00058 apart, against 253/200's 0.00013 - both inside the thousandth. 239 x 189 is the LARGEST pair under 191 that passes; 229 x 181 is the most exact and was rejected for being smaller still. WHAT IS LOST: at 3840x2160 the box was 506 x 400 device px, which is the small galaxy's own world extent at 1:1, and a smoke check pinned that. It is now 478 x 378 and the property is gone. It was a CONSEQUENCE of the box's size and never a requirement of the drawing - colonyinset.map_rect fits 128:91 isotropically and takes min(w/128, h/91), which no 1:1 relation enters - so the check now asserts the rule it was an instance of and v3_projektstatus.md records the loss. THE DRAWN MAP SHRINKS 5.5 %: 257 x 183 -> 243 x 173 at 1080p and 514 x 365 -> 486 x 346 at 2160p. Width still binds at every resolution, so the letterbox stays on the vertical axis and gets smaller. planet_output absorbs the 14 px this box gave up, as _lower_band_note says it always does.
_list_height_note: 634, AND IT IS DERIVED FROM THE SPRITE STEP - 8 September 2026, was 605. The list holds ten rows at every resolution (COLSUM::_list_col[10], colsum.cpp:348), so the row band is the window divided by ten and the figure step is the largest whose 28*step fits that band. At 605 the band was 81 device px at 2560x1440 and step 3 needs 84, so 1440p fell to step 2 and its figure columns filled 59 % of what the original's fill - against 79 % at the other two. THE CLEARANCE IS THE +8 ON TOP OF THE +21: the cell plate is a 1 px line and 46 of the 54 figure masters carry ink on canvas row 0 (measured over the whole set), so a figure blitted at the band's top would paint over the plate's top line. The bottom line needs nothing - every master has at least 3 transparent rows below its ink, the same measurement the row clip already rests on. So the rule is band >= 28*step + 1, and the smallest list that yields steps 2/3/4 under it is 638 cutout px = 634 typed plus the 2 px BLEED per side. Bands 63 / 85 / 127 with 6 / 0 / 14 px spare below the figure. THE 29 PX CAME OUT OF THE LOWER BAND'S HEIGHT and not out of the list_band rail, which stays at the master's own 28 (see _gaps_note): the four band boxes go from y 725 h 220 to y 754 h 191. WHAT THAT COST, MEASURED BY RENDERING AT ALL THREE RESOLUTIONS RATHER THAN BY ARITHMETIC ON BOX HEIGHTS: nothing. The sidebar still draws its six rows with no ink on the box edge and no label touching its value; planet_output still draws five; the description still wraps to five lines and uses 138 of 260 px at 1440p. AND THE GALAXY INSET DOES NOT MOVE AT ALL: colonyinset.map_rect fits 128:91 isotropically and WIDTH binds, so the drawn map is 257x183 / 342x243 / 514x365 at both heights and only the vertical margin shrinks, 21 -> 12 px at 1080p. It would start shrinking below a 183 px cutout.
